key_insight: PhysMoDPO closes the gap between diffusion-based text-to-motion models and physically-executable humanoid trajectories by optimizing generated motions with a learned preference objective that trades off fidelity and physical plausibility.
problem_solved: Diffusion-generated motions look realistic but often become unrealistic or unstable after conversion to robot/executable trajectories by Whole-Body Controllers (WBCs); the paper addresses how to modify generated motions so they remain faithful to the original intent while being physically feasible under WBCs.
method: Start from text-conditioned diffusion motion samples and convert them to executable trajectories via a Whole-Body Controller to expose physical mismatches.
Train a learned preference model that scores motions by a balance of fidelity to the original generation and compliance with physics/WBC outcomes.
Optimize the generated motion samples (PhysMoDPO) using preference-guided updates so final trajectories remain stylistically faithful while being physically plausible and executable.
impact: Enables reliable transfer of high-quality generative motion models to character animation and real robot control by producing motions that survive controller constraints—reducing manual retuning and improving realism in deployment.
